content.title: About
content.content: Monterey cheese is a semi‑hard American cheese made from pasteurized cow’s milk. It has a mild, slightly sweet flavor and a creamy texture, melts well, and is commonly used in grilled dishes and casseroles.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The cheese is named after the city of Monterey, California, where it was first produced in the early 20th century.
Traditional Monterey is aged from 2 to 12 months; longer aging gives a sharper taste.
It is often used in the classic British dish “fish‑and‑chips” as an alternative to cheddar.
The cheese melts easily, making it popular for sauces, soups, and pizza.
In the United States Monterey cheese is one of the most popular choices for burgers.

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: Monterey cheese provides a good amount of calcium, essential for bone and tooth health.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Its protein contributes to muscle maintenance and satiety.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamin B12 and riboflavin, which support energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Phosphorus and zinc
items.content: These minerals play roles in metabolism and immune health.

items.title: Probiotic cultures
items.content: Fermentation creates beneficial bacteria that can support gut flora.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Contains lactose, so people with intolerance should limit consumption.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: The cheese can be salty; excess sodium may increase blood pressure risk.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to casein.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Monterey cheese is calorie‑dense, so portion control is advisable, especially on weight‑loss diets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Monterey cheese can be sliced, grated into salads, added to sandwiches, used in casseroles, sauces, and on pizza. It is also frequently melted in grilled cheese sandwiches.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cheese in its original packaging or an airtight container in the refrigerator at 2‑4 °C. For longer storage it can be frozen, though the texture may change.

content.title: About
content.content: Mixed salad greens, raw is a ready‑to‑use blend of various leafy vegetables such as romaine, spinach, radicchio, arugula and lettuce. The product is sold dry, un‑cooked and intended for fresh preparations.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: A typical blend contains 5–7 different leaf types, providing a range of flavors and textures.
The green colour comes from chlorophyll, which also has antioxidant properties.
Restaurants often use mixed greens to quickly assemble salads and side dishes.
Leafy greens contain more vitamin K than most other vegetables.
Some blends include micro‑greens, harvested at an early stage and exceptionally nutrient‑dense.

items.title: Rich in vitamins A and C
items.content: Leafy greens provide carotenoids and vitamin C, supporting immune function and vision.

items.title: High in folate
items.content: Folate is essential for DNA synthesis and is especially important for pregnant women.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Mixed greens are virtually calorie‑free, making them ideal for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Dietary fiber for digestion
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy bowel movements and helps maintain satiety.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Phytonutrients such as lutein and zeaxanthin protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Raw leafy vegetables can carry Salmonella or Listeria; thorough washing before consumption is recommended.

items.title: Asteraceae allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to certain members of the aster family found in the blend.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: If the mix is not certified organic, pesticide residues may be present; rinse under running water before use.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use mixed salad greens as a base for fresh salads, bowls, wraps, smoothies, or as a garnish for meat dishes. Before serving, rinse the leaves, spin dry, and optionally toss with a light dressing.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the blend in its original packaging or an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0–4 °C. Once opened, it stays fresh for 5–7 days. Discard if you notice a sour smell or soggy spots.

content.title: About
content.content: Chocolate‑flavored wheat cereal is a ready‑to‑eat breakfast made from whole wheat grains, enriched with natural cocoa and sweeteners. It has a smooth texture, a sweet chocolate aroma, and provides lasting satiety.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Wheat is one of the oldest cultivated grains, grown by humans for over 10,000 years.
The chocolate taste comes from natural cocoa powder rather than artificial flavors.
The cooked cereal retains most of wheat’s dietary fiber, which supports digestion.
In some countries the cereal is served with milk, in others with yogurt or fresh fruit.
Wheat cereal is often included in sports nutrition for its high carbohydrate content.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Provides a slow release of energy, helping to maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: Rich in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion and contributes to a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Contains iron and B‑vitamins
items.content: These micronutrients support hemoglobin formation and nervous system function.

items.title: Antioxidants from cocoa
items.content: Cocoa powder supplies flavonoids that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: Thermally processed cereal is suitable for children and people with sensitive digestion.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: People with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity may experience adverse reactions.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Some versions contain added sweeteners; choose sugar‑free options if you monitor blood sugar.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The product can be calorie‑rich due to cocoa and sugar; portion control is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Eat the cereal straight from the pack, add milk, plant‑based milk, or yogurt. Top with berries, nuts, or banana if desired. For a thicker consistency let it sit for a few minutes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the package in a dry, cool place away from direct sunlight. After opening, reseal tightly to prevent moisture absorption. Follow the shelf‑life date printed on the packaging.
